reason: The wet methane needs preparation for its cold store, and the methane liquefier is the natural equipment for it.
expectation: I expect the plant to dry and liquefy the methane for storage, though I don't know whether a separate drying step is needed.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen also needs its own store, but I chose to follow the warm wet reactor output first.

effect: The liquefier produced the methane store and satisfied the drying and cooling goal in one step; I will now store oxygen separately.
reaction: The result is clear, though I am curious how the moisture was removed.
reason: Oxygen needs its own cold store and this is the only remaining combination.
expectation: I expect the oxygen liquefier to produce a separate liquid oxygen store.

effect: The oxygen store completes the second goal and confirms the two stores are separate.
reaction: It is satisfying to finish the fuel and oxidizer pair, but the result is very brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing the methane connected the preceding reactor work to a practical fuel supply for the return journey.

leastWorthwhile.text: The oxygen step was straightforward but produced only a terse confirmation, with little to discover about the storage system.

surprise.text: The wet methane became a dry cold store in a single action; I had expected there might be a separate drying step and remain curious how it was done.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: each gas had a matching liquefier, though the mechanics of drying were not explained.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the return preparations and the ice investigation develop, although this chapter itself offered little decision-making beyond ordering two obvious actions.
